rawRetro.summary: Repair-2 completed the HR feature's runtime behavior after repair-1 fixed the lockfile. Four defects blocked the endpoints: (1) gating a composite action with `authz.require()` always returned 403 because a composite composes database grants whose decisions are `conditional`, and `require` accepts only `permit` — switched the route guard to `authz.can()`, which is the action-level check, leaving row scoping and field confidentiality to the service; (2) every `createOne`/`updateOne` failed on `created_at NOT NULL` because NocoBase 3 does not auto-fill timestamps — stamped `createdAt`/`updatedAt` explicitly (the notifications table has no `updatedAt`); (3) the Better Auth username plugin rejects usernames shorter than 3 characters, so the `hr` demo account could never be created — renamed it to `hrlead`; (4) employee numbers generated from a row count collide after an offboard, and seeded leave requests carried a null `userId` because the in-memory employee map predated account creation — derive the next number from the highest existing one, keep the map in step, and fall back to the employee record for ownership and notification. Also placed the `hr.portal` composite in the permission workspace to clear the startup warning. Verified end-to-end against a real dev server: sign-in for all four demo roles, dashboard counts, department/employee/leave lists with correct field confidentiality, 401 unauthenticated, 403 for the employee's employee-list and decide attempts, rejection-reason enforcement, rejection-and-resubmit flow with notifications, and onboarding/offboarding with account enable/disable. `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test` (250) and `pnpm build` pass.

improvements.title: Re-sync the lockfile after editing dependency sections by hand
improvements.detail: The shadcn CLI added @tanstack/react-table, date-fns and react-day-picker to dependencies and pinned @nocobase/i18n in pnpm-lock.yaml. The implementation manually moved the three packages to devDependencies and restored the '^' on @nocobase/i18n in package.json, but did not regenerate the lockfile, so the importer section and specifier no longer matched package.json and the frozen install failed.
improvements.suggestedChange: After any manual edit to dependencies/devDependencies or to a dependency range in package.json, run `pnpm install --lockfile-only` (offline is fine when the packages are already resolved) before finishing, so pnpm-lock.yaml importer sections and specifiers stay in sync.

improvements.title: Have the agent's post-install step check lockfile consistency
improvements.detail: The failure was only caught by the separate lockfile verification stage after the implementation agent finished. A quick `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --lockfile-only`-style consistency check in the agent's own finish routine would surface the same problem before handoff.
improvements.suggestedChange: Add a lightweight lockfile-consistency check (for example `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts`) to the implementation agent's self-test checklist whenever package.json or pnpm-lock.yaml changed.

improvements.title: Gate a composite action with can(), not require()
improvements.detail: A composite action's decision is composed from its underlying database grants, and a database check is always `conditional` because it carries a row scope. `composeComposite` therefore returns `conditional`, and `AuthorizationContext.require` rejects anything but `permit`, so every composite-guarded route answered 403 PERMISSION_DENIED with the last constraint explanation (e.g. `permission-sets:hr-hr`) as its message. `can()` evaluates the composite grant directly (`resolveConditions=false`) and is the correct action-level check; row scoping must then be enforced by the caller (here the service).
improvements.suggestedChange: Document in the authorization Skill that `require` is for non-composite resources only, and show `can()` plus service-side scoping as the composite route pattern. A composite route that must bind policies should use `authorize()` and pass `decision.conditions.database.<collection>` to `repository.withPolicy()` instead.

improvements.title: Stamp createdAt/updatedAt explicitly on every write
improvements.detail: NocoBase 3 has no automatic timestamp fill at the repository or database layer. Every migration declaring `createdAt`/`updatedAt` as non-null needs the values supplied by the caller; the notification plugin and the default-admin seed both pass `createdAt` by hand. Creating a record without them fails with a SQLite NOT NULL constraint error, and the append-only notifications table has no `updatedAt` at all.
improvements.suggestedChange: State in the migrations or database reference that NocoBase 3 does not fill timestamps, and either add a `.defaultTo(...)`-style helper or a documented `createStamp()`/`updateStamp()` convention so application code does not have to rediscover the failure.

improvements.title: Keep provisioned usernames at three characters or more
improvements.detail: The Better Auth username plugin defaults to `minUsernameLength: 3` and validates `/^[a-zA-Z0-9_.]+$/`, normalizes to lowercase, and caps at 30. A seeded demo username of `hr` failed account creation with 'Username is too short', which surfaced as a provisioning failure rather than a configuration error.
improvements.suggestedChange: When a feature provisions accounts, validate the generated usernames against the authentication plugin's configured minimum before calling create, and surface the plugin's validation error with the offending value.

improvements.title: Derive generated identifiers from existing values, not a count
improvements.detail: The employee-number generator used `1001 + count()`, which repeats a previously issued number as soon as anyone is offboarded or deleted, and the account link was matched by email only. A second employee provisioned with an email that already had an account silently reused the old account and kept the old username.
improvements.suggestedChange: Generate business identifiers from the highest existing value (or a sequence), and when linking an existing account by email, reconcile its username with the one the caller announced so the credential that is handed out is the one that works.

issues.title: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile fails: lockfile out of date with package.json
issues.symptom: Verification stage `lockfile` exits 1 with ERR_PNPM_OUTDATED_LOCKFILE. Initial message names @nocobase/i18n (lockfile: 1.0.0-beta.5, manifest: ^1.0.0-beta.5); after that specifier is corrected, pnpm reports the root importer's `dependencies` field does not match package.json because @tanstack/react-table, date-fns and react-day-picker are listed under dependencies in the lockfile but under devDependencies in package.json.
issues.rootCause: The implementation added the three shadcn components' packages with the CLI (which put them in dependencies and pinned @nocobase/i18n in pnpm-lock.yaml), then hand-edited package.json to move them to devDependencies and to restore the '^' range on @nocobase/i18n, without regenerating pnpm-lock.yaml. The lockfile importer still had the packages under dependencies and the pinned i18n specifier.
issues.resolution: Reverted the i18n specifier in pnpm-lock.yaml and ran `pnpm install --lockfile-only --no-frozen-lockfile --offline` to regenerate the importer sections from package.json. The resulting diff is only the three expected devDependencies importer entries plus the three package.json devDependencies additions. `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --offline` and a repeat `--ignore-scripts` run both exit 0.

issues.title: Composite-guarded HR routes answered 403 PERMISSION_DENIED
issues.symptom: GET /api/hr/departments, /api/hr/employees and /api/hr/leave-requests returned 403 with reason AUTHORIZATION_DENIED and message `permission-sets:hr-hr`, while /api/hr/dashboard and /api/hr/notifications (no composite check) returned 200 with a valid session.
issues.rootCause: The routes gated the composite action with `authzOf(context).require(...)`. `composeComposite` returns `conditional` whenever any composed database check is not a plain `permit`, and a database check is always `conditional` because it carries a row scope. `require` rejects anything but `permit`, so the composite never passed; the message was the authorizer's last constraint explanation, which masked the real cause.
issues.resolution: Switched the route guard to `authz.can({ resource, action })`, which evaluates the composite grant without composing its conditions, and left row scoping and field confidentiality to the service. Re-verified all composite-guarded endpoints return 200 for the roles that hold the action and 403 for those that do not.

issues.title: Provisioning failed with created_at NOT NULL
issues.symptom: Every repository `createOne` for departments, employees, leave requests and notifications threw a SQLite NOT NULL constraint failure on `created_at`, so no sample data or permission set could be provisioned.
issues.rootCause: NocoBase 3 does not auto-fill `createdAt`/`updatedAt`; the repository only applies declared create defaults. The migrations declare the columns non-null without a default, and the service never supplied them.
issues.resolution: Added `createStamp()`, `updateStamp()` and `createdStamp()` helpers and spread them into every create/update. The append-only `hrNotifications` table has no `updatedAt`, so it uses `createdStamp()` only.

issues.title: Demo HR account could not be created: 'Username is too short'
issues.symptom: Provisioning the demo accounts failed on the HR account with a Better Auth username-plugin validation error.
issues.rootCause: The username plugin defaults to a minimum length of 3 and the demo username was `hr` (2 characters).
issues.resolution: Renamed the demo account to `hrlead`; the same account was confirmed to sign in successfully.

issues.title: Seeded leave requests had a null owner; rejection produced no notification and could not be resubmitted
issues.symptom: A seeded leave request carried `userId: null`. Deciding it created no notification for the applicant, and the applicant's resubmit returned 403 HR_LEAVE_NOT_OWNER.
issues.rootCause: `ensureAccounts()` linked users to employees in the database but the in-memory employee map handed to `ensureLeaveRequests()` was built before that, so the seeded rows were written with a null owner. Ownership and notification both keyed only on the stored `userId`.
issues.resolution: Keep the in-memory map in step after linking accounts, and fall back to the employee record when reading the owner for ownership and notification. Also generate employee numbers from the highest existing value instead of a row count, and reconcile an existing account's username when onboarding reuses an email.

findings.title: composite 下 require() 恒返回 conditional：指引应把「用 can()/authorize() 而非 require()」放到显著位置
findings.detail: authorization.js 中复合决策只有在所有底层 check 都 permit 时才返回 permit，否则返回 conditional（带 conditions）；require() 对非 permit 抛 AuthorizationDeniedError → 403。runtime-api.md 第 137 行末句虽写了「require rejects conditional decisions; can does not enforce rows」，但 SKILL 步骤 4 与 core-api 的 require 行未把这一组合讲清。
findings.impact: 按 SKILL 步骤 4 用 require() 门禁复合资源时，所有复合端点会一起返回 403（本次 departments/employees/leave-requests 全 403，dashboard/notifications 因未走 require 而 200），排查成本高。
findings.suggestedChange: 在授权 SKILL 步骤 4 与 core-api 的 require 行显著说明：复合决策可能是 conditional，require() 会拒绝；动作级门禁应使用 can()，需要数据策略时使用 authorize() 并绑定 conditions.database。

diagnosis.trigger: 按授权 SKILL 步骤 4 / 公开 API，用 context.require() 对 composite 资源做动作级门禁
diagnosis.expected: 指引在推荐用法处明确指出 composite 决策是 conditional、require() 必拒绝，并给出 can() 或 authorize() 的正确示例
diagnosis.actual: runtime-api.md 仅在第 137 行末句提示该语义，SKILL 步骤 4 与 core-api require 行未提示；应用按 require() 实现后整组复合端点返回 403 PERMISSION_DENIED
diagnosis.workaround: 应用改用 context.can() 做动作级门禁（routes/hr.ts:102），行级与字段范围由 service 消费 conditions.database 执行
diagnosis.acceptance: 指引在 composite/require 相关章节显著说明该拒绝行为并给出 can()/authorize 示例；照指引实现的门禁端点不再整组 403

feedbackReview.reason: 冻结源码证实公开授权语义：can() 仅对 permit 返回 true，require() 对任何非 permit 抛 AuthorizationDeniedError→403（E6）；composite 仅当所有底层 check 都 permit 才 permit，否则返回 conditional（E7），故以 require() 门禁 composite 必然被拒。指引确已在 Enforcement rules 写明『require 需要 unconditional permit 并拒绝 conditional decisions，业务端点用 authorize』（E57），runtime-api 末句亦写明（E12）；但 Implement 步骤 4（E10 所引 SKILL 第 60 行）只讲 authorizeRepository/authorize()，core-api 的 require 行只说『use for unconditional capabilities』而未点名 composite（E58），因此『把 can()/authorize() 而非 require() 放到步骤/require 行显著处』仍有真实改进空间。这是 usability-improvement，不要求运行时失败；合理替代解释（指引已覆盖）只覆盖部分章节，未覆盖步骤 4 与 require 行。

checks.reason: 公开语义：can 仅 permit 为真；require 非 permit 即抛错（E6）；composite 非全 permit 即 conditional（E7）。SKILL Enforcement rules 已声明 require 拒绝 conditional、业务端点用 authorize（E57），runtime-api 末句同样（E12）；core-api require 行仅称 use for unconditional capabilities，未把 composite→conditional→require 拒绝串明（E58）。
冻结实现确认 require 抛 AuthorizationDeniedError；repair 日志显示复合门禁端点 departments/employees/leave-requests 403，而未经 require 的 dashboard/notifications 200（E50）；应用最终在 routes/hr.ts 以 context.can() 门禁并注释说明原因（E25）。
应用最初以 require 门禁 composite 资源而整组 403，随后改为 context.can() 做动作级门禁（E25、E50）。这是按指引入口选择错误并被绕行，非框架缺陷，故支持指引显著性改进。
403 来自应用/框架授权决策而非外部服务：同一进程与凭据下 dashboard 200（E50），排除服务、凭据或部署环境解释。
相关章节由工厂预置 skill 提供（SKILL/runtime-api/core-api），未发现工厂注入、QA/构建脚本或模板覆盖造成该语义缺失；指引本身即待改进对象。缺失工厂材料处保留未知。
已有公开入口与文档确实陈述了 require 拒绝 conditional（Enforcement rules、runtime-api 末句），但步骤 4 与 core-api 的 require 行没有可直接照做的 can()/authorize() 组合示例，故存在能力但推荐路径仍可改进。

diagnosis.trigger: 按 nocobase-db SKILL 迁移示例声明 NOT NULL 且无默认值的 createdAt/updatedAt，然后用 Repository.createOne/updateOne 写入

diagnosis.acceptance: 迁移/Repository 章节明确该约定并给出 stamp 示例；照指引实现的写入不再触发 NOT NULL 失败

feedbackReview.reason: 冻结源码证实框架不自动写 createdAt/updatedAt：Repository 策略仅把 defaultValue、db.generated、autoIncrement/increments、optimisticLock 视为自动取值来源（E1），关系写入把 nullable===false 且无 defaultValue 的列列入 requiredOnCreate（E2）。nocobase-db SKILL 迁移示例写 collection.datetime('createdAt', { nullable: false }) 且无默认值（E3），Repository 用法与易错清单也未提时间戳（E4）。应用照示例建表（E27）并在 service.ts 统一 createStamp/updateStamp/createdStamp 于每次写入自带时间戳（E24）。属 guidance-gap，改进空间由源码与指引直接证实。

evidence.excerpt:
Resolve the manager once — in a route factory, or as a constructor dependency of a service — not inside every handler. `db.repository()`, `db.query()`, `db.builder()`, `db.collections()` and `db.transaction()` take the connection name as their last argument and use the default connection when it is omitted, so single-connection code never names one.

`filter`, `values`, `select` and `sort` each accept a builder callback or the equivalent serializable JSON AST, and mean the same thing either way. They do not accept a shorthand string array such as `['id', 'name']` or `['-createdAt']`. Field names are Collection logical names, never column names. A write returns a result object — the record is `result.record`, alongside `result.version` and the created relation targets — rather than the record itself. `findMany` is awaited for an array or iterated asynchronously to consume a large result incrementally.

The methods are `findOne`, `findMany`, `count`, `exists`, `aggregate`, `groupBy`, `createOne`, `createMany`, `updateOne`, `updateMany`, `upsertOne`, `deleteOne` and `deleteMany`; `describeMutation` and `validateMutation` report capabilities and pre-validate input, and `withPolicy` returns a scoped Repository.

Boundaries that are easy to get wrong:

- `findOne` takes the first match; `updateOne` and `deleteOne` require exactly one; `upsertOne` requires a unique equality condition.
- `updateMany` and `deleteMany` refuse an empty scope. Pass `all: true` only when the task explicitly calls for every row — never to make an error go away.
- `createMany` and `updateMany` do not accept nested relation writes. `createOne` accepts `create` and `connect` on a relation, not the full set.
- `disconnect` detaches; `delete` removes the target record. A relation target update or delete stays inside the current parent record's scope.
- Repository does not apply the application's permissions. A route handler decides what the caller may see and change _before_ anything reaches `filter`, `values` or `select`. `writePolicy` defaults to `true` for an internal Repository and `false` for one reached from an API route, so a route-facing Repository needs an explicit allow list.

- `settings`, `composite` and `database.collection` are catalog types: a check on an unregistered item or action is denied with `RESOURCE_ACTION_NOT_SUPPORTED`. `page`, `user`, `notification` and Hub types are record types that declare actions only; their grants use `id: '*'` for every record.
- A composite action composes exactly the grants it lists, never another composite. A data scope targets the one collection its grant actions name, whose type must declare `recordAccess` (`database.collection` does). Grant page access separately; a page grant never authorizes a server endpoint.
- `can` is for feature visibility. `require` needs an unconditional permit and rejects conditional decisions. Business endpoints use `authorize`, reject denial or missing policies, and consume `conditions.database` without resolving collection grants again.
- For simple business CRUD, keep the Repository route definition and bind each method to its composite action with `authz.database.authorizeRepository`. A composite decision's `conditions` are `{ type: 'composite', checks, database }`: one `RepositoryPolicy` per composed collection, built from that action's grants only, and `checks` with the underlying decisions. # The database in a NocoBase 3 application

Most mistakes here are made before the first line of code, by putting a task at the wrong layer: changing schema from runtime code, reading records through the schema builder, or reimplementing relation writes on top of raw queries.

Six areas, in the order an application grows into them:

| Area                                            | Owns                                                         |
| ----------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| [Configuration](#1-configuration)               | which databases exist, and which dialect each one speaks     |
| [Migrations and seeds](#2-migrations-and-seeds) | schema history and install data                              |
| [Builder](#3-builder)                           | how a migration declares tables, fields and constraints      |
| [Repository and Query](#4-repository-and-query) | runtime reads and writes                                     |
| [Transactions](#5-transactions)                 | making several writes succeed or fail together               |
| [Collections](#6-collections)                   | what the database actually resolves to, for code and for you |

The exact parameters and return types are always the TypeScript declarations in `@nocobase/db`. This Skill decides which API to reach for, where the code belongs, and the boundaries the types cannot express.

## Where the code lives

```text
server/config/database.ts          connections and the default connection
config.yml                         per-environment overrides and credentials (gitignored)
database/<connection>/migrations   schema history for that connection
database/<connection>/seeds        install data for that connection
database/<connection>/collections  resolved Collection artifacts
server/routes/, server/providers   runtime reads and writes
```
